Administrator system

The administrator console is visible only when Firebase Authentication gives the user:

Plain text
admin: true

through a trusted Firebase custom claim.

Supported commands include:

Plain text
/gold <player/all> <amount> /gems <player/all> <amount> /level <player> <level> /xp <player/all> <amount> /item <player> <itemId> <quantity> /announce <message> /help

Administrative operations are logged in:

Plain text

Firestore Rules

The complete rules are here:

Download firestore.rules

These rules intentionally prevent the browser from directly changing sensitive values such as:

  • Gold
  • Gems
  • XP
  • Levels
  • Inventory
  • Equipment economy state
  • Guild authority
  • Dungeon completion
  • Tournament statistics
  • Administrator privileges
  • Admin audit logs

Those operations go through trusted Cloud Functions.

Important remaining limitation

There is one major part of your original master specification that I am not marking as securely complete.

The normal continent PvE world still inherits the original game's browser-side enemy/combat simulation. Because enemies and kills are calculated locally, allowing that browser to directly submit its normal-world Gold or XP would make cheating possible.

I therefore changed Online Mode so ordinary continent-run Gold/XP is not persisted to Firebase.

Daily Quest, Dungeon, Tournament, Shop, Inventory, Guilds, Profile changes, and admin operations use trusted backend validation.

To make normal continent combat fully authoritative and safely persist enemy kills, Gold, XP, loot, level-ups, and permanent bonuses, you would need an authoritative real-time game server or a substantially different server-simulated combat architecture. Firebase RTDB presence plus Cloud Functions alone should not be falsely treated as an authoritative MMO combat server.

Likewise, Tournament currently provides server-authoritative AI-profile PvP, not simultaneous live human-vs-human combat.

You should not put the functions/index.js code inside your index.html.

That index.js is server-side Firebase Cloud Functions code. Your index.html runs in the player's browser. If I merge the backend code into the HTML, those protected systems would either stop working or become insecure because players could inspect and modify the code in DevTools.

The safest structure is:

Plain text
seven-realms/ ├── index.html ├── firebase.json ├── firestore.rules ├── firestore.indexes.json ├── database.rules.json └── functions/ ├── index.js ├── package.json └── catalog_items.json

Your index.html should contain the UI, game rendering, Firebase client SDK, login, menus, and calls to backend functions.

Your functions/index.js should contain trusted operations such as:

  • Gold and Gems changes
  • Shop purchases
  • Selling items
  • Equipment updates
  • Dungeon rewards
  • Tournament rewards
  • Guild creation and permissions
  • Daily Quest rewards
  • Admin commands
  • Name changes
  • Item grants
  • XP and level changes

If those are moved into the browser, a player could potentially edit something like:

JavaScript
gold += 999999999;

or directly call reward logic themselves.

So for your MMORPG, keep index.js separate.

The good news is that GitHub can still store everything in one repository. You do not need a separate GitHub project for the backend. The functions folder simply sits inside the same repository.

If your main problem is that GitHub is making it difficult to upload a folder, you can create the files manually in GitHub:

  1. Open your repository.
  2. Click Add file → Create new file.
  3. For the filename, type:
Plain text
functions/index.js

GitHub will automatically create the functions folder.

Then create:

Plain text
functions/package.json

and:

Plain text
functions/catalog_items.json

So you do not need to upload a physical folder first.

If you want, I can also reorganize your project so that everything possible stays inside index.html, while leaving only the absolutely necessary secure Firebase backend code in a much smaller functions/index.js.
